hypothesis: Setup-context census (sub-agents/shared/tools/setup_census.py) proved EXP-0007 and EXP-0008 were inert: setup CARD options have cardId == None, so heuristics reading option.cardId rank every option equally and the stable sort reproduces baseline order. Setup options identify their card by area == HAND (2) plus index into obs.current.players[yourIndex].hand, whose entries are Card objects with .name. Implement ONLY the opening Active choice: when select type is CARD and context is SETUP_ACTIVE_POKEMON, resolve each option through hand[option.index].name and choose by replay priority Dreepy, Munkidori, Budew, Meowth ex, Fezandipiti ex last, falling back to existing _choose_card logic when any option cannot be resolved. SETUP_BENCH_POKEMON is deliberately untouched: the census shows minCount 0 maxCount 2 and the baseline already benches every Basic offered, so bench priority is a no-op. MAIN-phase PLAY, ATTACH, Trainer, Ability, Attack, Evolve, and damage-target logic unchanged.
expected_effect: Census over 10 baseline games: baseline sends Fezandipiti ex to Active on 4 of 4 offers and Dreepy on only 6 of 10, while 87 curated replays show Dreepy dominant in wins (31) and Fezandipiti ex neutral (4W/4L). Ranking Fezandipiti ex last should shift the opening Active card. Decision traces MUST show SETUP_ACTIVE_POKEMON differences; entirely MAIN/MAIN means inert again and immediate rejection.
reason: Inert candidate, caused by a wrong engine fact supplied in the worker prompt. Hand entries are Card(id, serial, playerIndex) with no .name attribute; the name must be resolved via all_card_data() keyed on hand[index].id. The patch read getattr(hand[i],'name',None), got None, and _choose_setup_active_card returned None on every setup selection, so the agent fell back to baseline _choose_card. Direct A/B on identical observations: 20/20 SETUP_ACTIVE_POKEMON selections identical to baseline. Trace 124 differences, all MAIN. Screening 101/200 (50.5%, p=0.888) measured nothing. The setup_census card_name() helper masked the flaw by falling through to an id lookup.
